summary: This component detects when a user types the famous Konami code (up-up-down-down-left-right-left-right-b-a) on their keyboard and triggers a fun animation of a meerkat running across the screen for 3 seconds. It listens for keydown events, tracks progress through the sequence while ignoring modifier keys and repeated key presses, and resets if the wrong key is pressed—unless that key happens to be the first key of the sequence, in which case it keeps momentum.

explanations.19: This creates a Set of arrow key names for quick lookup later, because checking if something is in a Set is faster than checking an array.
explanations.46: If the key is a single character (like 'b' or 'a'), convert it to lowercase so 'B' becomes 'b'; otherwise return it as-is (like 'ArrowUp' stays 'ArrowUp'). This normalizes user input to match our KONAMI_CODE expectations.
explanations.52: progressRef is a reference that persists across renders and holds our current position in the Konami code sequence—we use ref instead of state because we don't need a re-render when it changes.
explanations.68: The repeat flag is true when a key is held down and fires multiple events automatically; we ignore these to prevent a held arrow key from accidentally advancing multiple steps.
explanations.78: We increment our progress tracker by 1, moving forward one step in the Konami code sequence.
explanations.84: If the pressed key doesn't match what we expect, reset progress to 0—unless it's the first key of the Konami code, then set it to 1 since they might be starting fresh.
